lead: Intrauterine fetal death is death of the fetus in the uterus after the limit of viability: WHO ≥ 28 wk or ≥ 1000 g (UK stillbirth from 24 wk). Earlier loss is managed as a miscarriage. About half have no cause found.
f: Unexplained: about 50%, the commonest single group · Maternal: pre-eclampsia, diabetes, infection (malaria, TORCH, syphilis, listeria), anaemia, thyroid disease, thrombophilia (APS), Rh isoimmunisation · Fetal: anomalies, FGR, TTTS, hydrops, feto-maternal haemorrhage · Placenta and cord: abruption, insufficiency, cord accident

sc: IUFD with fever and rigors → Malaria: blood film
Recurrent IUFD with DVT and miscarriages → Antiphospholipid syndrome

f: Reduced or absent movements; breasts soften · Uterus small for dates, SFH stops rising · Real-time ultrasound with no heart motion is diagnostic (second operator if possible) · Later signs: Robert sign (gas in the fetal heart, about 12 h, earliest X-ray sign), Spalding sign (overlapping skull bones, about 7 days), maceration

tr: No heart on a Pinard or hand Doppler does not prove death: only a real-time scan confirms

f: Mother now: FBC, clotting + fibrinogen, urine protein, LFT, RFT, glucose/OGTT, malaria film, TORCH, syphilis, blood group (Rh-negative: Kleihauer), TFT if symptoms · At 6 wk: thrombophilia, APS · Fetus: detailed scan; karyotype · After birth: autopsy and placental histology
DIC (hypofibrinogenaemia) is the most serious: about 10% in the first 3 wk, about 30% if retained over 3 wk · Infection and sepsis (especially after ROM) · PPH · Grief and depression

Most choose induction: mifepristone 200 mg, then misoprostol 36–48 h later · Misoprostol: under 27 wk 200 µg 4–6-hourly; 27–28 wk 100 µg 4-hourly; over 28 wk 25 µg vaginal 6-hourly or 25 µg oral 2-hourly · Previous CS: lower doses; 2 or more CS or classical scar: Foley + oxytocin or CS · Expectant: 85% labour within 3 wk; clotting 2–3 times a week · Deliver now with ROM, fever, DIC, abruption or PE · Avoid ARM; CS only for usual indications; epidural only with normal clotting

sc: IUFD with bleeding and low fibrinogen → Correct DIC, deliver now
IUFD with two previous CS → No routine misoprostol

f: See, hold and name the baby · Suppress lactation: cabergoline 1 mg once · Rh-negative: anti-D 500 IU within 72 h after Kleihauer · Review at 6 wk: results, cause, grief · Next pregnancy: folic acid, early booking, OGTT, aspirin if placental cause, serial growth scans, birth at term
